text: One Aimparency server holds many graphs: created there, mirrored from Git, or a local checkout
description:
Felix 2026-11-12: Aimparency is built for many graphs. Everyone just hosts Aimparency and manages users there. People can sign up and create graphs. For Commons Hub: a server that makes it easy for people to create accounts and graphs, and where GitHub repos can be mirrored (the .bowman part at least). Using repos that are already checked out is an option for self-hosting.

Storage, decided by Felix 2026-11-12: git still persists and versions the graphs. The graphs on a server are proper repos, not just a .bowman folder; in some cases a repo holds only .bowman, but version controlled.

Committing, decided by Felix 2026-11-12:
- Very important: no commit per action. Committing is done in the UI.
- The author is the default git author. Commits often contain changes from several people. If you host your graph and give users access, it is basically you who is on the commit. No further system for change authors for now.

Three kinds of graph on one server:
- created on the server by an account (a new repo on the server); needs the account's permission to create graphs
- added from a remote URL, by any account. Committing and pushing back to that remote should work too.
- a local checkout the server admin adds (self-hosting; ideas stay tracked next to the code)

Pushing to a remote, Felix 2026-11-12: users configure SSH keys, a key per account, and select the key per repo. With that one can add repos by remote URL.

Recommended by Claude, not confirmed by Felix: the server makes the key pair and shows only the public key, which the person adds on the remote (on GitHub as a deploy key for that one repo, with write access). Private keys are then never uploaded and never leave the server, and a break-in exposes single repos instead of whole GitHub accounts. A remote added without a key is read-only.

Each graph has a host URL, which is to .bowman what the remote URL is to git. The MCP connects to one host URL for one graph.

Today: a hosted server serves exactly one project (AIMPARENCY_PROJECT); the API identifies a project by its absolute path on the server; mirroring exists as "open from Git URL", read-only (git-repository-cache.ts). Committing in the UI exists: the header prompts a commit, the commit dialog commits chosen files inside .bowman and can push (f4a00b04, 37a09590, 3ec0cdee); in hosted mode it needs the admin role today.

Assumed by Claude: the owner of a graph and accounts with write access may commit and push; the API names a graph by an id instead of a server path.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: When a private repository becomes a space in one dialog, teams keep their intention network next to their code without making the repository public.
When updating a hosted server is one click for its admin, hosted servers run current code instead of drifting behind main.

status.comment: Built 2026-11-13 (b2b6fd2a, e5d3bf4a). One server described by a server directory (AIMPARENCY_SERVER_DIR: server.json, accounts.json, graphs.json) replaces hosted, read-only and local mode. Graphs are addressed by slug (/g/<slug>); created on the server as a git repository of their own, added from a Git URL (only .bowman cloned, pushed back with an SSH key the server makes), or a checkout listed with `pnpm graphs add`. Commit and push in the UI for owner and writers; the git author falls back to server.json gitAuthor. Evidence: backend tests auth.test.ts, one-port-server.test.ts (the server over real HTTP on a private port), graphs/remote-graph.test.ts (clone, key, commit, push, pull against a bare repository); `pnpm check` 25 of 25; the running dev stack still opens this repo by path. Not seen by me: the UI with accounts on in a browser, because starting an instance was refused. Question for Felix: run `pnpm start --setup`, answer yes to other people, and try creating a graph and adding one from a Git URL. Does it work and look right?
